title: Module Documentation: Unit Fractions from Dense Sets
content: Erdős Problem #47 (SOLVED): if $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ has $\sum_{a \in A} 1/a > \delta \log N$, must there exist $S \subseteq A$ with $\sum_{n \in S} 1/n = 1$? Bloom [2021] proved YES with threshold $\sum 1/a \gg (\log\log\log N / \log\log N) \cdot \log N$. Liu-Sawhney [2024] improved to $(\log N)^{4/5+o(1)}$. Erdős conjectured $(\log\log N)^2$ suffices; Pomerance showed this is optimal. The formalization axiomatizes Bloom's theorem and the Liu-Sawhney improvement.
mathContext: Given $A \subseteq [N]$ with $\sum_{a \in A} 1/a \geq f(N)$, does $\exists S \subseteq A: \sum_{s \in S} 1/s = 1$? The threshold $f(N)$ is between $(\log\log N)^2$ (conjectured optimal) and $(\log N)^{4/5}$ (best known).

title: Imports and Setup
content: Imports Mathlib's $\texttt{Finset}$, $\texttt{Rat}$, and $\texttt{Real.log}$ for working with finite subsets of $\mathbb{N}$, rational arithmetic, and the natural logarithm. The $\texttt{open Finset Filter}$ gives access to $\texttt{Finset.sum}$ and filter-based asymptotic reasoning. The namespace $\texttt{Erdos47}$ scopes all definitions.
mathContext: Working in $\mathbb{Q}$ avoids real-number complications for exact reciprocal sums $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a}$. The threshold $\delta \log N$ uses $\texttt{Real.log}$.

title: Reciprocal Sum
content: The function $\texttt{reciprocalSum}(A) = \sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a}$ computes the sum of reciprocals over $\mathbb{Q}$ for exactness. The guard $a = 0 \mapsto 0$ handles the edge case. This is the central measure of density in Erdős's conjecture: sets with $\sum 1/a > \delta \log N$ are 'dense' in a harmonic sense.

title: Unit Fraction Sum Property
content: A set $S$ has the unit fraction sum property if all elements are $\geq 1$ and $\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$. Such decompositions are called Egyptian fraction representations of 1. Classical examples include $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{6} = 1$ and $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{12} = 1$.
mathContext: $\texttt{HasUnitFractionSum}(S) \iff (\forall n \in S,\; n \geq 1) \wedge \sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$. Related to Egyptian fractions: $1 = \frac{1}{n_1} + \cdots + \frac{1}{n_k}$ with $n_i$ distinct.

title: Contains Unit Fraction Subset
content: The existential property: $A$ contains a nonempty subset $S \subseteq A$ with $\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$. The nonemptiness condition excludes the trivial empty-sum case. This is the conclusion that Erdős's conjecture (and Bloom's theorem) establishes.

title: Interval $\{1, \ldots, N\}$
content: The set $\{1, \ldots, N\}$ encoded as $\texttt{Icc1}(N) = \{k+1 : k \in \{0, \ldots, N-1\}\}$ via $\texttt{Finset.range}$ and image. This avoids 0 and gives the natural domain for reciprocal sums.
mathContext: $\texttt{Icc1}(N) = \{1, 2, \ldots, N\}$. The full reciprocal sum is $H_N = \sum_{a=1}^N \frac{1}{a} \sim \log N + \gamma$ (Euler–Mascheroni constant $\gamma \approx 0.5772$).

title: Dense Subset Definition
content: A subset $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ is $\delta$-dense if $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a} > \delta \log N$. Since $H_N \sim \log N$, this means $A$ captures a positive fraction $\delta$ of the total harmonic mass. The full set satisfies $\sum 1/a \sim \log N$, so $\delta$-density requires keeping a constant proportion of harmonic weight.

title: Erdős's Conjecture (Formal Statement)
content: The formal statement of Problem #47: for every $\delta > 0$, there exists $N_0$ such that for all $N \geq N_0$ and all $\delta$-dense subsets $A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$, there exists $S \subseteq A$ with $\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$. This captures both the density condition and the finiteness threshold.

title: Bloom's Theorem (2021)
content: Thomas Bloom proved Erdős's conjecture in 2021: $\texttt{ErdosConjecture47}$ holds. His proof uses a sophisticated combination of the Hardy–Littlewood circle method, exponential sums, and structural results about the additive energy of sets with large reciprocal sums. This resolved a problem open since at least the 1960s.
mathContext: $\texttt{bloom\_theorem} : \texttt{ErdosConjecture47}$. Bloom's proof shows that for any $\delta > 0$, if $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a} > \delta \log N$, then some $S \subseteq A$ satisfies $\sum \frac{1}{n} = 1$.

title: Bloom's Quantitative Bound
content: Bloom's proof gives an explicit threshold: there exists $C > 0$ such that $\sum_{a \in A} \frac{1}{a} \geq C \cdot \frac{\log \log \log N}{\log \log N} \cdot \log N$ suffices. The triple-logarithmic factor comes from Bloom's iterative density increment argument. This is much weaker than $\delta \log N$ but gives an explicit quantitative result.
mathContext: $\exists C > 0 : \sum \frac{1}{a} \geq C \cdot \frac{\log \log \log N}{\log \log N} \cdot \log N \Rightarrow \exists S \subseteq A,\; \sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$.

title: Liu–Sawhney Improvement (2024)
content: Mehtaab Liu and Ashwin Sawhney dramatically improved Bloom's quantitative bound: for any $\varepsilon > 0$, $\sum \frac{1}{a} \geq (\log N)^{4/5 + \varepsilon}$ suffices for large $N$. This is a polynomial improvement over Bloom's triple-log bound, using refined structural decompositions and Fourier-analytic methods.
mathContext: $\forall \varepsilon > 0,\; \exists N_0 : \sum \frac{1}{a} \geq (\log N)^{4/5+\varepsilon} \Rightarrow \texttt{ContainsUnitFraction}(A)$. Compare: Bloom needs $(\log N)^{1-o(1)}$; Liu–Sawhney needs $(\log N)^{4/5+o(1)}$.
